headline: LLM agents turn natural-language requests into executable omics analyses
label: Llm Agents For Omics Analysis
summary: Four preprints and one published CellVoyager study now pair LLM agents with executable tools, provenance tracking, and benchmark evaluation.
synthesis: The common thread is LLM-driven agents that convert natural-language instructions or expression data into executable omics workflows. EnsAgent is a tool-ensemble multi-agent system that combines consensus clustering with Proposer-Critic expert annotation to label spatial transcriptomics data robustly. stMCP exposes spatial analysis through a Model Context Protocol server with local tool execution and benchmarks. OmicClaw runs reproducible natural-language multi-omics analysis over the OmicVerse ecosystem with provenance tracking. CellVoyager autonomously generates and runs scRNA-seq analyses in Jupyter and is evaluated on the 76-study CellBench benchmark. A BioBERT sliding-window classifier for manuscripts containing computable phenotypes is more peripheral, reporting 95% accuracy. What is new is the layering of executability, provenance, and evaluation around generative components rather than generation alone.
